reasoning_traces.think:
The contrast ratio validator enforces WCAG AA compliance by computing luminance-based ratios between foreground and background tokens. It operates on a binary exit code system where 1 indicates failure and 0 success. This primitive is foundational to GSI’s accessibility inference engine. Token file synchronization detects inconsistencies between tailwind.config.ts and design-tokens.css, particularly in color definitions like obsidian. These discrepancies can lead to rendering divergence in UI elements. The theme surface system defines two hardcoded themes—dark and paper—used conditionally based on component context, not globally toggled. This structure implies that GSE must manage multiple implicit theme states within a single application lifecycle. Together, these primitives define a dual regime: one of static validation (contrast) and another of dynamic assignment (themes). Failure modes include non-compliance in contrast checks and drift in token definitions, both of which compromise visual consistency and accessibility.
